title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale
excerpt: Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases. With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. Here, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

ai.why: Developers could leverage LLMs to add formal guarantees to their projects more efficiently.

title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
excerpt: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. We introduce StreamEval, a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation spanning five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. StreamEval comprises 300 scripted test cases lasting 15-300s, each specifying initial assets, incrementally arriving multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Performance is assessed along four evaluation dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination, instantiated…

ai.summary: StreamEval is a benchmark that evaluates interactive streaming video generation models across five tasks—avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing—using 300 scripted test cases lasting 15‑300 seconds each.
ai.why: It gives developers a standardized way to measure real‑time video generation capabilities, helping guide model improvements and product integration.

title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
excerpt: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. Whether memory can drive genuine continual learning remains an open question. In this paper, we introduce Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL), arguing that memory should be judged by whether it improves future actions, not merely what it retrieves. MCCL has three main parts. First, a three-axis taxonomy organizes…

ai.summary: The paper presents Memory‑Centric Continual Learning, a framework where agents use an external memory not just for retrieval but to drive ongoing weight updates for long‑term learning.
ai.why: Offers a strategy for building agents that can adapt over time, valuable for products requiring continual improvement after deployment.

title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
excerpt: Multimodal code intelligence connects the symbolic world of programs with the visual world their execution creates. Interest in this capability is burgeoning, as models are increasingly asked to produce charts, webpages, animations, and semi-structured documents. Recently, proprietary models have pushed far ahead, producing interactive artifacts even from a text description or a screenshot alone. Yet their data and training remain closed, and open progress is held back by the quantity and quality of available data and by the pipelines and methods for producing it. Quality is the harder of the two, since a sample must be correct as a program, well built, and above all visually right once…

meta.org: NLP Group of The University of Hong Kong

ai.summary: PrismaCoder is an open‑source multimodal code‑intelligence system that generates code and visual artifacts by decomposing tasks into rubric‑based sub‑steps.
ai.why: It provides developers with a free tool to experiment with multimodal programming assistance, potentially reducing reliance on closed‑source models.

title: CulturalRiddles: A Multicultural Benchmark of Riddles
excerpt: As LLMs expand their language coverage, evaluating how well they understand and represent diverse cultures becomes increasingly important. However, many benchmarks remain English-centric, with limited cultural coverage and a focus on factual knowledge over its application in real-world cultural contexts. We propose CulturalRiddles, a benchmark of original, culturally grounded riddles created entirely by humans through a participatory community effort, spanning 62 cultures (45 countries, 51 languages). These riddles are deeply rooted in their respective cultures and require abductive and compositional reasoning, alongside detailed factual and social knowledge, language skills, and an…

ai.summary: CulturalRiddles is a benchmark of human-created riddles spanning 62 cultures, 45 countries, and 51 languages, designed to evaluate LLMs' understanding of diverse cultural contexts beyond factual knowledge.
ai.why: Useful for developers aiming to reduce cultural bias and improve the multilingual cultural competence of their models.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality
excerpt: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) grounds large language models in external knowledge. Modern pipelines combine embedding, chunking, retrieval, reranking, query augmentation, context compression, and agentic verification, yet these techniques are typically evaluated one at a time. It remains unclear whether their isolated gains survive composition, whether retrieval quality and answer faithfulness favor the same design choices, and whether conclusions from small corpora hold at large scale. We pre-declare three hypotheses and introduce LASAGNA, an open-source framework for controlled RAG evaluation. We test 450 configurations across eight benchmarks and corpora ranging from 5K to 200K…

ai.summary: A paper titled “Retrieval Augmented Generation Compositionality” investigates how combined RAG components (retrieval, reranking, augmentation, etc.) interact at scale and affect answer faithfulness.
ai.why: Provides insights for developers building RAG pipelines about which components synergize best.

title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
excerpt: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time. Storing the state at lower precision therefore lets more sequences share an accelerator. Existing state quantizers round the state after every generated token and report that four bits lose accuracy unless the bit width is raised or the model is fine-tuned.\par We introduce PACE, a post-hoc four-bit state quantizer. PACE rounds the state only once every few generated tokens, as chunked kernels already do once per chunk during prefill, and keeps the tokens generated in between in a small buffer…

ai.summary: The paper PACE proposes a post‑hoc four‑bit quantizer for the recurrent state of linear‑attention language models, reducing memory while preserving accuracy.
ai.why: Enables more efficient inference of large models on limited hardware, useful for developers deploying high‑throughput services.

title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills
excerpt: Agent Skills improve LLM agents by making task knowledge reusable across sessions. Learning transferable Skills requires evidence about a procedure and its conditions of use, which a successful task attempt can leave untested. We introduce Socratic Skill Learning (SSL), which interleaves expert teaching with Student practice. An Educator guides investigation while the Student remains the sole environment operator and Skill author, able to question, test, and adapt advice. To test reuse beyond the learning task, we construct SkillTransferBench, with 35 task families and 408 executable cases, pairing public variation specifications with held-out evaluation in fresh solver sessions. On the…

ai.summary: Socratic Skill Learning (SSL) interleaves expert teaching with student practice, allowing LLM agents to acquire and adapt reusable skills through questioning and testing.
ai.why: Enables creation of modular, transferable agent capabilities that can be reused across different tasks.

title: Building AI Research Teams for Autonomous Discovery of Linear Attention Architectures
excerpt: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. However, realizing this design requires more than diverse backgrounds. When experiments are costly, a team can test only a limited number of ideas, thereby creating the need to balance exploration and exploitation when selecting a subset of researchers to propose and execute new experiments. Furthermore, each result should shape what the team tries next. We…

ai.summary: The authors propose building AI research teams of heterogeneous agents to autonomously discover linear attention architectures, using orthogonal expertise to avoid local minima during costly experiments.
ai.why: It suggests a framework for developers to orchestrate multiple AI agents for collaborative model‑architecture search, potentially accelerating innovation.

title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
excerpt: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. The scarcity of contact-rich bimanual manipulation data and the increased complexity of coordinating contacts make developing a generalist bimanual tracker particularly challenging. Therefore, we present 1) DONIC, the first generalist bimanual tracker jointly trained across operation categories and human-motion sources, together with 2) BiHOI, a multi-view dataset of 1,575 sequences spanning 229 objects and emphasizing sustained bimanual interaction, where…

ai.summary: DONIC is introduced as the first generalist bimanual dexterous tracking controller trained jointly on human demonstration data to handle coordinated two‑hand manipulation tasks.
ai.why: It expands the range of robotic manipulation capabilities developers can leverage, enabling more complex dual‑hand tasks without task‑specific training.

title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
excerpt: A login screen that appears after a tap on Sign in is expected; the same screen after a tap on View order is an attack. For GUI agents, safety is therefore a property of the transition rather than of the screen, and a monitor that inspects only screens can be defeated by reusing a legitimate one. Judging a transition requires an expectation of what should have followed the action. Existing GUI world models provide one, but they output it as text, code, or images, so checking it against the observed screen requires a second model to judge the two. We argue that a world model meant for verification should instead predict in the space in which observations are encoded, and present LGWM, a…

ai.summary: The paper proposes using world models as runtime verifiers for GUI agents, checking the expected transition after an action rather than just the resulting screen, to detect attacks that reuse legitimate screens.
ai.why: It offers a concrete method to improve safety of autonomous GUI agents, which developers can integrate into testing pipelines.

title: Scaling in Games: Continued Pre-Training For Embodied Agents In Diverse Virtual Worlds
excerpt: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. We investigate this question through a controlled study of continued pre-training (CPT) across three axes: data volume, diversity, and model size. Our 120 training configurations span four model sizes from 0.8B to 27B, six data budgets from 50 to 1,600 hours, and five mixtures ranging from Minecraft-only data to diverse multi-world corpora. We assess performance and generalization using three-level…

ai.summary: A systematic study of continued pre‑training (CPT) for embodied agents across data volume, diversity, and model size shows scaling benefits in virtual worlds with varied visual styles and dynamics.
ai.why: Insights guide developers on how to allocate compute and data when building more capable agents for simulation environments.

title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
excerpt: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. We introduce Future Chunk Prediction (FCP), an auxiliary objective jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising that predicts temporally separated chunks without access to the intervening visual context. Drawing supervision directly from training videos, FCP requires no additional pretrained visual encoder and leaves autoregressive inference…

ai.summary: Future Chunk Prediction (FCP) is added as an auxiliary loss to autoregressive video diffusion models, encouraging them to predict temporally distant frames rather than just local continuity.
ai.why: Improves video generation models' ability to capture true scene evolution, useful for developers building generative video tools.

title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
excerpt: Agent learning is shifting from learning from human data toward learning through interaction with the world. However, scaling such learning directly in real-world computer systems is challenging and can introduce substantial security risks. We therefore propose Agent World Model in the Wild (WildAWM), a scalable pipeline for synthesizing controllable environments and tasks for training general computer-use agents (CUAs). Whereas existing approaches typically specialize in a single agent interaction interface, we construct executable environments that jointly support graphical user interfaces, model context protocol services, and command-line interfaces, allowing agents to flexibly combine…

ai.summary: The paper introduces WildAWM, a pipeline that creates synthetic, controllable computer environments and tasks to train general-purpose computer‑use agents without needing real‑world systems.
ai.why: Provides a safer, scalable way to develop agents that can operate software, reducing security risks of direct system interaction.

title: Cache Engineering for Agents
excerpt: Large Language Model (LLM) agents can handle increasingly complex tasks, navigating long trajectories of observations and actions. As these trajectories grow, key-value (KV) cache I/O and storage become the dominant cost. Trajectories can also exceed the LLM's maximum context length, requiring control over active cache growth. Prior work uses context engineering to reduce cache size by trimming or summarizing history. However, modifying the trajectory prefix invalidates subsequent cached states and triggers costly re-prefilling of retained context. Task accuracy can also suffer when too little context is retained to limit re-prefill costs. We propose cache engineering as a new scheme. It…

ai.summary: The authors propose cache‑engineering techniques for LLM agents to manage key‑value cache growth, addressing costs and context‑length limits during long‑trajectory tasks.
ai.why: Helps developers build more efficient agents that can handle extended interactions without exceeding model context windows.

title: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
excerpt: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present GRSE, Group-Relative Skill Evolution, which assigns behavioral credit by comparison: inspired by GRPO, it executes each question several times under the same skill libraries and contrasts the executions to credit agent--skill pairs, with structured diagnosis of failures. On HotpotQA and LoCoMo with two open-weight actors, GRSE outperforms…

ai.summary: GRSE (Group‑Relative Skill Evolution) introduces a credit‑assignment method that compares skill performance across multiple runs to identify which agent's skill should be updated in cooperative language‑model teams.
ai.why: It offers a more accurate way for developers to evolve multi‑agent systems without weight updates, improving collaborative behavior.

title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
excerpt: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. In this work, we observe that sparsifying attention in different layers and at different denoising steps affects final-video fidelity to substantially different degrees. Yet the identities of the most sensitive layer-step pairs remain nearly unchanged across inputs. Building on these findings, we propose Allocating Layer-step Latency by Output Tests (ALLOT), a training-free sparsity allocation method…

ai.summary: The paper presents a training‑free method to allocate block‑sparse attention in video diffusion transformers, dynamically adjusting sparsity per layer and denoising step to preserve video fidelity while reducing compute.
ai.why: Developers can adopt this technique to speed up video generation models without sacrificing quality, lowering hardware requirements.

title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
excerpt: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the current state, Anticipate action effects, Plan a feasible course, Act through an interface or body…

ai.summary: The authors define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) that combine multimodal reasoning with physical actuation, and analyze the differences when transitioning from computer‑use to robot‑use scenarios.
ai.why: Understanding these differences helps developers design agents that can seamlessly move between virtual tool use and real‑world robotics.

title: AgenticRoboRL: Bringing Coding-Agent Post-Training to Agentic Robotics
excerpt: Agentic robotics systems combine planners with robot harnesses to perform complex manipulation tasks. Recent work improves these systems through better harnesses and external memory, but relies on powerful closed-source models as planners and does not improve the planners' own capabilities. In contrast, coding agents have improved substantially by post-training the model itself. We therefore investigate whether post-training can also improve robot planners. However, applying it across robot harnesses requires accommodating different execution mechanisms, including VLA skill invocation and control-code generation. To this end, we introduce AgenticRoboRL, a framework for post-training robot…

ai.summary: AgenticRoboRL explores post‑training of coding‑agent style models to enhance robot planner capabilities, aiming to improve manipulation performance without relying on closed‑source models.
ai.why: Shows a path for open‑source robotics teams to boost planner quality via fine‑tuning, reducing dependence on proprietary APIs.

title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
excerpt: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. SpatialScout comprises 80 diverse indoor scenes containing 3,140 target objects. Given an object inventory, RGB observations, camera calibration, and camera poses, agents control a camera to explore each scene and estimate object centers in a shared coordinate frame. The…

ai.summary: SpatialScout is a benchmark for testing vision‑language model agents on active object‑level 3D mapping, featuring 80 indoor scenes with 3,140 target objects for autonomous exploration.

title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
excerpt: Post-hoc image explanations usually show where a model looks using spatial heatmaps or indicate which channels matter using global channel scores. These separate views are limiting for multispectral data because channel relevance is often spatially localized and physically meaningful. We introduce Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a full-grid attribution method over position-channel players (g,c). For each spatial position, SSI fixes the observed surrounding context, defines a conditional game over the channels at that position, and applies the Shapley value to this local game. The result is a full spectral-spatial attribution matrix rather than a single heatmap or a global channel…

ai.summary: The authors propose Spectral-Spatial Interpretation (SSI), a full-grid attribution method that assigns importance to each position‑channel pair in multispectral images, enabling localized channel relevance analysis.
ai.why: It provides developers of vision models for multispectral data a more precise debugging tool than separate spatial heatmaps or global channel scores.

title: Real In, Real Out: What If We Only Use Real Data for Scene Text Editing?
excerpt: Aiming to modify textual content while preserving the original style, Scene Text Editing (STE) has significant practical value in many applications. STE typically requires paired images before and after editing for training. However, recent approaches rely heavily on synthetic paired data and complex disentanglement strategies. They struggle to faithfully capture the diversity and complexity of natural scenes, often producing artifacts or hallucinations. In this work, we challenge the common practice and investigate whether STE can be driven by turning each real sample into its own paired supervision. Concretely, we explore multiple ways to disrupt the original image (e.g., Crop, Shuffle…

ai.summary: The paper challenges synthetic data reliance in scene text editing by training solely on real paired images, aiming to preserve style while editing text without hallucinations.
ai.why: Developers can build more reliable text‑editing tools that work on natural images without needing extensive synthetic datasets.

title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
excerpt: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone. Recent work recovers the hidden reasoning by replaying encrypted blocks across models. It somehow works, but it breaks the providers' terms of service, so it is not something a product can be built on…

ai.summary: TraceForge proposes using an LLM to generate detailed reasoning traces as training data for another model, enabling distillation that preserves chain‑of‑thought information.
